identity.title: Benchmarking Empirical Privacy Protection for Adaptations of Large Language Models

problem.claim: Assess practical privacy risks when adapting LLMs with differential privacy, across data distributions, adaptation methods, and privacy regimes.

gap.claim: The practical effectiveness of DP adaptation remains unclear because pretraining overlaps and interdependencies with adaptation data may undermine privacy despite theoretical guarantees.

contributions.claim: A systematic benchmark of empirical privacy risks under DP LLM adaptation, varying adaptation-data distribution, methods, and privacy regimes.
An analysis of how distribution proximity to pretraining and parameter-efficient fine-tuning relate to practical privacy vulnerability.
A proposed framework for holistic privacy assessment across the full LLM pretrain–adapt pipeline.

stated_novelty.claim: The work extends privacy assessment beyond adaptation privacy toward structured evaluation across the full pretrain–adapt pipeline.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that, at the same theoretical guarantee, practical privacy risk is higher when adaptation data is closer to the pretraining distribution, even without direct overlap.
The authors report that parameter-efficient methods such as LoRA provide the highest empirical privacy protection for OOD adaptation data.
The authors report evaluating privacy vulnerability with robust membership inference and canary data extraction across exact-overlap, IID, and OOD settings.

narrative_sequence.summary: DP offers theoretical guarantees for sensitive LLM adaptation, but practical protection may be weakened by pretraining–adaptation relationships.
The study evaluates robust membership inference and canary extraction while varying data distribution, adaptation method, and privacy regime.
Privacy risk increases as adaptation data approaches the pretraining distribution, including without direct overlap.
LoRA performs best empirically for OOD data, and the authors propose broader pretrain–adapt privacy assessment.

source_observation.claim: The abstract compares practical privacy at a fixed theoretical guarantee across adaptation-data distributions and distinguishes direct overlap from distributional proximity.

lessons.interpretation: Separating theoretical guarantees from distribution-sensitive empirical risk makes hidden privacy conditions explicit.
lessons.application: When presenting a privacy method, report matched-guarantee evaluations across overlap, IID, and OOD data, explicitly distinguishing direct overlap from distribution shift.
lessons.exception: This framing may be unsuitable when the deployment distribution is fixed and cannot be meaningfully varied or characterized.

unknowns: The abstract does not provide attack success rates, sample sizes, numerical privacy budgets, or details of the evaluated adaptation methods and regimes.
The proposed holistic framework’s structure and evaluation procedure are not specified.
The basis for the reported comparison of LoRA with other methods is not detailed.
